A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same W2S generalization work. Their main text, Appendices A–E, equations, 13 figures and three tables are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic regression experiments and evaluations on UTKFace, ColoredMNIST and SST sentiment classification in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments, including measured risks, PGR, OPR, dimension estimates and label-noise analyses.

M1.justification: The teacher fitting, pseudo-label generation and student fitting procedures remain unchanged, including the ridge objectives and sentiment finetuning losses. The substantial revisions concern their analysis and diagnostic measurements.

E1.justification: Synthetic regression, UTKFace and ColoredMNIST coverage is retained. Appendix E.3 replaces the description of full-sentence SST-2 with a dataset subsampled from SST parse trees, retaining the same sample counts and results. The PDFs do not establish whether sentence/phrase coverage changed or the existing dataset description was corrected.

E2.justification: The weak teacher, strong SFT baseline, strong ceiling and evaluated teacher architectures are retained. Appendix E.2 corrects a CLIP-B32 mention to DINOv2-s14, which v3 already identifies as the student in its setup and Table 2; this is not a comparator replacement.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 revises the stated correlation-estimation procedure: the Gaussian sketch changes from dimension d_s by D to N by (d_s+p), with oversampling and truncated column-pivoted QR specified. This is a reported procedure correction without evidence of reruns; experimental split sizes, training budgets and performance metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same sample-size and feature-discrepancy sweeps, synthetic noise-regime comparisons, and injected-label-noise analyses on UTKFace, ColoredMNIST and SST. No empirical ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both specify standard-deviation error bars over 40 synthetic runs and 10 UTKFace runs. The plotted uncertainty and other repeated-run or statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–13 retain identical plotted content, and Tables 1–3 retain their numerical entries. The reported empirical rankings and noise/discrepancy trends are unchanged; the revised analytical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 revise feature-coupling assumptions, specify S-based evaluation and condition the bias–variance decomposition on training inputs. Weak-teacher variance changes from sigma² d_w/n to sigma² d_w/(n-d_w-1), with corresponding strong-baseline and finite-sample bias corrections. PGR/OPR bounds and their optimizing sample sizes change substantially. Appendix B replaces Lemma 2 with a small-ball argument; Appendix C replaces the ridge bound and proof, adding fourth-moment and proportional-asymptotic conditions and changing the leading dependence from nN to n with an N-dependent correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the central claims: intrinsic dimension and teacher–student discrepancy explain variance reduction in W2S, with implications for relative performance and sample sizes. Their principal contribution statements are not redefined.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 changes the interpretation from non-monotonic PGR and OPR bounds sharing an optimal labeled sample size to a decreasing PGR bound and a separately optimized, non-monotonic OPR bound. Appendix C replaces the claim that increasing nN compensates approximation-related terms with the qualification that increasing N cannot eliminate inherited teacher parameter noise.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 clarifies and corrects the sketch dimensions, oversampling and QR implementation used for correlation estimation. It also revises SST construction to parse-tree subsampling while removing the explicit neutral-sentence filtering description. Other training and computing-resource disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 adds Mourtada (2022) for the revised inverse-covariance argument, removes Vershynin (2010), and removes Xue et al. (2025) and its representation-based W2S discussion. The broader research positioning and related-work coverage remain intact.

P1.justification: The overall outline, abstract, introduction and experimental narrative are retained. Focused reorganization moves the risk definition into Section 2.2 and finite-sample approximation-error definitions into Appendix B, alongside revised technical explanations, cross-references and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: All figure designs and table structures are retained. Appendix pagination and placement change, including Figures 7 and 9 moving earlier and Table 3 moving from page 50 to page 49; there is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially repairs the paper's central theoretical accounting: it corrects reference-model evaluation errors and finite-sample bias, states additional assumptions, replaces the inverse-covariance argument, and removes the ridge claim that more pseudo-labels can eliminate inherited noise. These are important gains for a theory-centered paper, despite narrower guarantees. Integration remains incomplete: Figures 1–4 retain earlier theoretical curves, including Figure 4's non-monotonic PGR bound, despite the revised formulas.
